paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. Proverbs 19 is a pile of short sayings, but they all lean the same way. Walk with integrity, get wisdom, and fear the LORD, because "The fear of the LORD leads to life" (Proverbs 19:23). Chasing money, flattery and shortcuts looks smart for about a minute, and then it falls apart like a cookie pulled out of the oven too early.

Now here's the part I love. Solomon, king of Israel (Proverbs 1:1), says it plainly: "Many plans are in a man's heart, but the purpose of the LORD will prevail" (Proverbs 19:21). I make plans ALL the time, friend. Plans are fine, but they're not the boss. So you can hold yours loosely and hold His purpose tight, because His is the one that stands.

And look at how wisdom gets built. "Listen to counsel and accept discipline, that you may be wise the rest of your days" (Proverbs 19:20). Wisdom grows when you stay teachable, forgive quickly, and are kind to people who can't pay you back, because "Kindness to the poor is a loan to the LORD, and He will repay the lender" (Proverbs 19:17). So today, baker, pick one thing to listen to, one offense to overlook, and one person to be kind to.
